newsitem.title: USA: NY State Electric unable to reach pact.
newsitem.headline: NY State Electric unable to reach pact.

text.p: New York State Electric & Gas Corp was unable to reach an agreement with the New York Public Service Commission staff on the pending restructuring case, commission spokesman David Flanagan said.
The deadline for reaching an agreement on changes in the company's late September filing in the commissions Competitive Opportunities Proceeding had been extended to Tuesday.
When the talks broke down, Flanagan said, commission regulations calling for a litigated proceeding became effective and intervenor testimony was accepted by the commission.
New York State Electric & Gas now has 25 days to respond to that testimony, Flanagan said, adding commission rules call for the proceeding to be completed in 90 days.

In response to questions about Flanagan's statement, the utility released a brief statement dated March 26 saying: "Discussions with PSC staff have not yielded an agreement. We remain hopeful that an agreement can be reached with various parties."
Spokesman Clayton Ellis said he can not go beyond the statement at this time.
New York State Electric & Gas is the only utility, out of the five required to file by October 1, 1996, to force a litigated proceeding.

New York State Consumer Protection Board Executive Director Timothy S. Carey described the agreements the staff has reached with Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc, Orange & Rockland Utilities Inc and Central Hudson Gas & Electric Corp as a "historic undertaking," pointing out the three utilities voluntarily gave up their monopoly status.
"You have to give the (commission) staff credit," he added.
Last week, the commission extended the deadline for an agreement with the fifth utility, Rochester Gas & Electric Corp, to April 8.
